note: Byte-frozen ontos/data (L2) embeddings: int, utf8-text, bool, list. Each case gives the datum, its L0 value (as {atom:hex}|{tuple:[...]} authoring notation), and the expected FULL ontos-codec-v1 encoding of that L0 value. A scalar embedding is Tuple(Atom(label), Atom(payload)); list is the structural embedding Tuple(Atom('list'), elem*). Canonical payloads: int = sign byte (00=nonneg, 01=neg) + big-endian minimal magnitude, with zero = single 0x00 and no leading zero bytes; utf8-text = valid UTF-8 verbatim (no normalization); bool = single byte 00=false / 01=true; list = ordered sequence, elements are arbitrary L0 values each already in its OWN canonical form (value-not-position rule), order and multiplicity are identity, empty list = Tuple(Atom('list')), the bare unlabeled Tuple(elem*) form is NOT a list. list is the non-arche structural fixture that discharges the agnosticism gate (ontos-data.md s7). The `hex` values were generated by the real ontos-codec-v1 encoder and are replayed by the codec vector-runner (encode(value)==hex AND decode(hex)==value) across go/rs/ts. Label bytes: int=696e74, bool=626f6f6c, utf8-text=757466382d74657874, list=6c697374. The 'reject' array holds L0 values that are valid at L0 but are NOT well-formed embeddings of the named 'kind' field: read<kind>(value) MUST reject each (recognition is partial and opt-in — ontos-data.md s1/s7). The reject DECISION is cross-language pinned here; the specific not-recognized error code stays implementation-local and diagnostic (unlike the codec's pinned reject codes). map (added 2026-06-01, §5.7): Tuple(Atom('map'), Tuple(key,value)*) — the 'map' label (bytes 6d6170) followed by arity-2 entry tuples, entries STRICTLY ascending by ontos-codec-v1 byte order on the KEY (order(A,B)=lexicographic(encode A, encode B), codec §6); duplicate keys forbidden (equal adjacent key encodings); keys and values are arbitrary L0 values with NO recursion into sub-embedding canonicality (a non-canonical-int key is accepted — map_noncanonical_int_key); empty map = Tuple(Atom('map')). The map hex were generated by the real ontos-codec-v1 encoder over the sorted canonical form. map is codec-version-relative (its order is ontos-codec-v1's). set (added 2026-06-01, §5.8): Tuple(Atom('set'), elem*) — the 'set' label (bytes 736574) followed by elements STRICTLY ascending by ontos-codec-v1 byte order on each element (codec §6); duplicate elements forbidden (equal adjacent encodings); elements are arbitrary L0 values with NO recursion into sub-embedding canonicality (a non-canonical-int element is accepted — set_noncanonical_int_elem); empty set = Tuple(Atom('set')). set is map's discipline without values (the unordered-unique sibling of list/map), codec-version-relative. int_2pow128 (datum 2^128) is a canonical int beyond a 128-bit host width: every core RECOGNIZES it identically because recognition is structural, while a binding over a bounded host integer (Rust i128) cannot MATERIALIZE it into its host type — a resource limit, not a non-recognition (read<kind>(int) reports it recognized; ontos-data.md s5.1, the int-layer analog of ontos-codec.md s3.1's limit_exceeded). It pins cross-core recognition agreement at the host-width frontier. decimal (added 2026-06-06, §5.9): Tuple(Atom('decimal'), int(mantissa), int(exponent)) — the 'decimal' label (bytes 646563696d616c) followed by two int children, the value mantissa × 10^exponent. Canonical iff a non-zero mantissa is NOT divisible by 10 (no trailing base-10 zero) and zero is decimal(int 0, int 0), with BOTH children canonical ints. Unlike list/map/set, decimal RECURSES into its children — a non-canonical-int child (decimal_noncanonical_int_mantissa) is rejected, the SCALAR discipline (contrast map/set, which accept a non-canonical-int member). decimal is codec-INdependent (its canonical form is purely structural), so the decimal_* hex are hand-authored Class A: the decimal tuple wrapper over the already-pinned int child encodings. decimal_2pow128_mantissa is the int_2pow128 analog one layer up — recognized by every core, materialized only by the unbounded (Go/TS) bindings. null (added 2026-06-13, §5.10): Tuple(Atom('null')) — the 'null' label (bytes 6e756c6c) with NO payload children (tuple arity EXACTLY 1), the single canonical spelling of present-but-no-value and its only inhabitant. Recognition is structural: label 'null' exact AND arity exactly 1; ANY payload (arity > 1, null_with_payload) is NOT a well-formed null (guardrail 1 — exactly one no-value, forever), as are the bare empty tuple, a bare atom, and a near-miss label. null is the empty-container shape with a new label (like list/map/set's empty form) and is codec-INdependent — its canonical form is fixed by structure alone, so the null hex is hand-authored Class A. null means present-but-no-value, NOT absence (absence stays structural — an absent map key; §5.10).

encode.name: utf8_leading_feff
encode.datum: "\uFEFFx" (a leading U+FEFF is content and is kept, ontos-internal#338)

encode.name: map_noncanonical_int_key
encode.datum: { int(000001): 0x00 } (non-canonical int key, accepted — no recursion)

encode.name: set_noncanonical_int_elem
encode.datum: { int(000001) } (non-canonical int element, accepted — no recursion)

encode.name: decimal_2pow128_mantissa
encode.datum: 340282366920938463463374607431768211456 × 10^0 (mantissa beyond i128 — recognized by all cores, materialized only by the unbounded bindings; the int_2pow128 analog at the decimal layer)

reject.note: magnitude has a leading 0x00 (non-minimal zero)

reject.name: int_leading_zero_magnitude
reject.note: magnitude has a leading 0x00 byte

reject.name: int_wrong_arity_3
reject.note: tuple arity 3, want 2

reject.name: int_label_not_atom

reject.name: int_payload_not_atom

reject.name: int_not_a_tuple

reject.name: int_on_bool_value

reject.name: bool_empty_payload
reject.note: empty payload

reject.name: bool_two_byte_payload

reject.name: bool_bad_byte

reject.name: bool_on_int_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed int read as bool

reject.name: text_invalid_utf8_ff

reject.name: text_lone_continuation

reject.name: text_on_bool_value

reject.name: list_bare_tuple
reject.note: a bare unlabeled tuple is not a list

reject.name: list_empty_tuple
reject.note: arity 0 — no label child

reject.name: list_not_a_tuple
reject.note: a bare atom (even the bytes of 'list') is not a list

reject.name: list_on_int_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed int read as list

reject.name: map_unsorted
reject.note: entries out of key order (encode(0x62) > encode(0x61), so 0x61 must come first)

reject.name: map_duplicate_key
reject.note: duplicate key 0x61 (equal adjacent key encodings)

reject.name: map_entry_arity_3
reject.note: an entry has arity 3, want exactly 2

reject.name: map_entry_arity_1
reject.note: an entry has arity 1, want exactly 2

reject.name: map_flat_interleaved
reject.note: flat key,value children are not arity-2 entry tuples

reject.name: map_unlabeled
reject.note: no map label — first child is an entry tuple, not Atom("map")

reject.name: map_empty_tuple
reject.note: arity 0 — no label child (the empty map is Tuple(Atom("map")))

reject.name: map_not_a_tuple
reject.note: a bare atom (even the bytes of "map") is not a map

reject.name: map_on_list_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed list read as map

reject.name: set_unsorted
reject.note: elements out of order (encode(0x62) > encode(0x61))

reject.name: set_duplicate
reject.note: duplicate element 0x61 (equal adjacent encodings)

reject.name: set_unlabeled
reject.note: no set label — first child is an element, not Atom("set")

reject.name: set_empty_tuple
reject.note: arity 0 — no label child (the empty set is Tuple(Atom("set")))

reject.name: set_not_a_tuple
reject.note: a bare atom (even the bytes of "set") is not a set

reject.name: set_on_list_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed list read as set

reject.name: decimal_trailing_zero_mantissa
reject.note: non-zero mantissa 10 is divisible by 10 (trailing base-10 zero); canonical is decimal(int 1, int 1)

reject.name: decimal_zero_nonzero_exponent
reject.note: zero mantissa with a non-zero exponent — zero is canonically decimal(int 0, int 0)

reject.name: decimal_noncanonical_int_mantissa
reject.note: mantissa child is shaped like an int but non-canonical (leading-zero magnitude); decimal RECURSES into its children (§5.9), so this is not a well-formed decimal (the scalar discipline — contrast map/set which accept a non-canonical-int member)

reject.name: decimal_mantissa_not_int
reject.note: mantissa child is a bare atom, not an int embedding

reject.name: decimal_wrong_arity_2
reject.note: tuple arity 2 — missing the exponent child (decimal is arity 3)

reject.name: decimal_not_a_tuple
reject.note: a bare atom (even the bytes of "decimal") is not a decimal

reject.name: decimal_on_int_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed int read as decimal

reject.name: null_with_payload
reject.note: arity 2 — a 'null' with a payload child; null is present-but-no-value, so ANY payload (arity > 1) is not a well-formed null (guardrail 1: exactly one inhabitant)

reject.name: null_with_two_payloads
reject.note: arity 3 — more payload, still not a null

reject.name: null_near_miss_label
reject.note: arity-1 tuple with the near-miss label 'nul' (bytes 6e756c) — the label must be exactly 'null'

reject.name: null_empty_tuple
reject.note: arity 0 — no label child (the null is the arity-1 Tuple(Atom('null')))

reject.name: null_not_a_tuple
reject.note: a bare atom (even the bytes of 'null') is not a null

reject.name: null_on_list_value
reject.note: cross-kind: a well-formed empty list read as null (empty list is Tuple(Atom('list')), a different label)
